pure-announcement.rationale: This is a new-tool release writeup that is entirely a METATRON feature rundown — model variant, sampling parameters, database schema, export formats, RAM requirement, GitHub link — and its only general ideas (local inference avoids exfiltration, an agentic tool loop) appear as one-line product positioning with no transferable mechanism.

duplicate.rationale: No nearest concept covers AI-assisted penetration testing or local-LLM security tooling; the overlap candidates (osv-format, siem-agentic-visibility-gap) address vulnerability data formats and SIEM logging.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The described tool is public on GitHub under MIT license, so every feature claim can be checked against the code.

durability.rationale: The content is spec-sheet detail — huihui_ai/qwen3.5-abliterated:9b, a 16,384-token window, temperature 0.7, a five-table MariaDB schema, 8.4 GB RAM — that will misdescribe the tool within months and carries no mechanism that outlives it.

actionability.rationale: The only action a reader can take is to install and run this specific product; nothing guides how to build or evaluate offline AI pentest tooling in general.

atomicity.rationale: The note is about exactly one thing — the METATRON tool and its feature set — and states it in a paragraph.
